what: DoorDash delivers food and groceries. Customers order through its app, couriers collect from restaurants and shops, and it takes a fee from the merchant and the customer. It owns Wolt in Europe and has acquired Deliveroo.
customers: Consumers ordering delivery, restaurants and retailers listing on the platform, and couriers who make the deliveries.
money: commissions and fees from orders on DoorDash, Wolt and Deliveroo
white-label delivery software for merchants and advertising on the app
moat: Density in each city: more couriers mean faster delivery, which brings more customers, which brings more merchants, and rivals must subsidise heavily to break in.
risks: Laws reclassifying couriers as employees would raise costs sharply
Operating margin is thin at about 5% despite large scale
Integrating Deliveroo across Europe is a substantial undertaking
Consumers cut delivery spending first when budgets tighten
opportunities: Revenue has grown about 28% a year for three years
Grocery and retail delivery raise order frequency and basket size
Advertising on the app is high-margin revenue from traffic it already has
watch: Total orders and gross order value, plus whether operating margin keeps widening.
